item.title: [Aaron Levie] 编程是窥见未来知识工作形态的一扇窗
item.description:
@levie · 查看 X 原推文 ↗

中文翻译

编程这件事，能让你提前看到大量知识工作未来会变成什么样。

对大多数工作来说，第一步是：我们过去大部分时间都在手动做调研、打字、创造价值（哪怕用的是数字工具），而很快，这些工作会变成我们去协调智能体来做。

再往后，当“协调”这一步本身也变得多余，或者拖慢了智能体能做的事，我们就会直接给智能体设定目标，让它们自己去优化，去替我们解决越来越大的问题。

乍一看，这好像只是编程领域才会发生的事，但实际上，由于能带来的生产力提升实在太大，很大一部分知识工作最终可能都会收敛到这种形态上。智能体会使用电脑、调用我们现有的工具或者自己写新工具，还会现场写代码，去解决更大范围的知识工作。

所以，哪怕今天某个任务看起来不直接是“编程”，它最终也可能变成跟编程沾边的事。制造业、建筑业、生命科学、材料科学、网络安全，等等等等。

当然，路上有个大障碍：很多这类工作目前还无法验证，所以人在其中的参与会比编程时更多。但随着模型能力越来越强，人能交出去的部分只会越来越大。

总之，多留意编程，你就能感受到工作未来要往哪儿走。

英文原推文

Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work.

The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing.

Next, as this step itself becomes redundant or slows down what agents are capable of, we will be giving agents goals to optimize against and they’ll go off on and increasingly solve larger problems for us.

This may at first blush look like something whose impact gets stuck with coding, but actually a large percentage of knowledge work may eventually just converge with this form factor due to the massive productivity gains that can be generated. Agents will use computers, leverage our existing tools or write new ones, and write code on the fly to solve larger swaths of knowledge work.

So even if a task today doesn’t seem to be “coding” directly, the task may eventually fold into being coding adjacent. Manufacturing, architecture, life sciences, material sciences, cyber, and on and on. One big hurdle in the way ultimately will be that much of this work remains non-verifiable, so humans will be even more in the loop than they are in coding. But the part that they can hand off will just get bigger and bigger over time as the models are more capable.

So in short, pay attention to coding and you’ll get a sense for where work is going.

item.title: [Thibault Sottiaux] GPT-6.2 上线计费出错，官方致歉并补偿
item.description:
@thsottiaux · 查看 X 原推文 ↗

中文翻译

GPT-6.2 上线时我们犯了个计费错误，导致大多数用户在使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 时被错误地少算了用量。

这个问题现在已经修复，所以同样的工作量会占用你套餐里更多的用量额度。跟上周相比，你在 GPT-6.2 Astra 上会快 40% 触达上限，在 Sol 上会快 25%。不过跟 6 Astra 和 6.1 Sol 比，这两个模型还是更耐用一些。其他模型没受影响，过去用量的差额我们也不会向你补收费用。

作为对这次失误的一点歉意，我们会给 Go、Plus、Pro 和 Business 的所有用户额外加一次可存的额度重置。

英文原推文

We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users.

We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan’s usage allowance. Comparing to last week, you will reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2 Astra and 25% faster on Sol. You should still see these go further in usage compared to 6 Astra and 6.1 Sol. Other models weren’t affected, and we won’t charge you for the difference on past usage.

As a small token to apologize for the mistake, we’ll be adding one banked reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business.

item.title: [Andrej Karpathy] 我让Claude用真实数据打造《文明》风格美国地图，45K行代码后成功了
item.description:
@karpathy · 查看 X 原推文 ↗

中文翻译

我让Claude用美国真实数据填充了一张《文明》风格的游戏地图。Opus 5.5下载并解析了大量公开数据，7小时45分钟后，写了4.5万行代码……它跑起来了 :)

- 31个真实数据源，包括人口普查局、经济分析局、劳工统计局、能源信息署、国家海洋和大气管理局、地质调查局、国防部、国家公园管理局、联邦航空管理局、联邦应急管理署、疾病控制与预防中心…… - 真实的海拔、土地覆盖、GDP、就业、发电厂、矿山、港口、机场、军事基地、公园、大学、货运流量、灾害；全部整合到一张25公里的六边形网格上。 - 数据被转换成《文明》的语言，比如金币产出就是GDP。城市的区域对应其真实产业特色：圣何塞有“校园”区，底特律是“汽车城”。市民就是真实劳动力：圣何塞每4个工人中就有1个是工程师、程序员或科学家，而全国是每14个中有1个。奇观根据公开规则选择，比如国家公园按游客数量，大学按研发支出，等等等等。 - 19种视角（收入、学历、信仰、灾害……），524个都市区的城市视图，还有9位顾问加一位探索者。探索者能把3100多个县的任意一列数据变成表格和散点图，并与地图联动。 - Claude决定跳过几个州和领地，抱歉 - 使用Claude Code桌面应用构建，Opus 5.5中等模式并开启ultracode。

部署在这里：https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 ，点“？”也有源码链接。我不太确定自己到底想做什么，但浏览和玩起来真的很有趣。也许可以扩展或做成游戏。不过我每周的Claude额度只剩一半了，所以得靠别人接手了 :D。Claude还做了一个预告片：

英文原推文

I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC... - Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid. - The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc. - 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map. - Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry - Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

item.title: [Peter Yang] AI产品最大挑战：人类跟不上AI的节奏
item.description:
@petergyang · 查看 X 原推文 ↗

中文翻译

AI产品面临的最大挑战之一，似乎就是让人类跟上AI正在做的事情。

电影《她》的结尾，AI们觉得人类太慢了，于是集体离开了我们——这个结局离现实似乎并不太远。

英文原推文

It seems like the one of the biggest challenges of AI products is just letting humans keep up with whatever the AI is doing.

That ending of Her where the AIs found humans too slow and collectively left us doesn't seem too far from reality.
